title: Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning
abstract: arXiv:2607.14192v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As recommender systems mature in the past few years, their optimization objectives have evolved from a primary focusing on short-term behavioral signals to a broader emphasis on long-term user engagement and retention. However, directly optimizing retention is difficult because return signals are sparse, delayed, and only partially attributable to earlier recommendations. Prior work has addressed this challenge with sequential modeling and reinforcement learning, but these approaches typically require task specific reward engineering, substantial computational overhead, and surface specific implementations that are difficult to generalize. In this paper, we present a unified, model-agnostic downstream reward framework for optimizing long-term user value in large-scale recommendation systems. First, we formulate the downstream reward learning problem and develop an offline screening framework to identify session level behaviors

translated_title: 通过模型无关的下游奖励学习优化长期用户参与度
translated_abstract: 摘要：随着推荐系统在过去几年的成熟，其优化目标已从主要关注短期行为信号演变为更广泛地强调长期用户参与度和留存率。然而，直接优化留存率很困难，因为回报信号稀疏、延迟，并且仅部分归因于早期的推荐。先前的工作通过序列建模和强化学习解决了这一挑战，但这些方法通常需要特定任务奖励工程、大量计算开销，以及难以泛化的表面特定实现。在本文中，我们提出了一个统一的、模型无关的下游奖励框架，用于优化大规模推荐系统中的长期用户价值。首先，我们形式化了下游奖励学习问题，并开发了一个离线筛选框架来识别会话级行为。
tldr: 本文提出了一种模型无关的统一框架，通过离线筛选和下游奖励学习，有效优化推荐系统中的长期用户参与度，解决了现有方法中奖励工程复杂和泛化性差的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a unified, model-agnostic framework that leverages offline screening and downstream reward learning to effectively optimize long-term user engagement in recommender systems, addressing the issues of complex reward engineering and poor generalization in existing methods.
